# gashe

```go
import "github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
```

Package gashe is a caching library: it stores results of expensive calls in a backend and protects callers from slow or failing dependencies with strategies built on top of it.

A Cache turns values into bytes with a Codec and stores them in a Backend. A strategy, such as Cached, is created once with its options and called with a key and a loader; it decides whether to answer from the cache or to run the loader.

<a name="ErrNotFound"></a>

```go
var (
    // ErrNotFound reports a miss: the key has no live entry.
    ErrNotFound = errors.New("gashe: not found")
    // ErrInvalidTTL reports a TTL the operation cannot accept, such as a negative one.
    ErrInvalidTTL = errors.New("gashe: invalid ttl")
    // ErrWrongType reports an entry that holds data the operation cannot use,
    // such as IncrBy on a value that is not an integer.
    ErrWrongType = errors.New("gashe: wrong type")
    // ErrInvalidOptions reports options that cannot work, such as a negative duration.
    ErrInvalidOptions = errors.New("gashe: invalid options")
    // ErrLockLost reports a lock that expired before its holder extended it.
    ErrLockLost = errors.New("gashe: lock lost")
    // ErrRateLimited reports a call over its rate limit.
    ErrRateLimited = errors.New("gashe: rate limited")
    // ErrCircuitOpen reports a call refused by an open circuit breaker.
    ErrCircuitOpen = errors.New("gashe: circuit open")
    // ErrOverloaded reports a load refused by Stampede.MaxLoads: every slot was taken
    // until ctx ended, or an old result could answer in its place.
    ErrOverloaded = errors.New("gashe: overloaded")
)
```

<a name="GetOrLoad"></a>
## func [GetOrLoad](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/getorload.go#L21-L27>)

```go
func GetOrLoad[V any](ctx context.Context, c *Cache, key string, o Policy[V], load func(context.Context) (V, error)) (V, error)
```

GetOrLoad returns the result stored under key, or calls load, stores its result and returns it; o says when a stored result is still good enough. Stored results are shared by every process that uses the same backend. Concurrent calls with the same key and type share one lookup and one load, when Stampede.SingleFlight is set; this sharing lives in the memory of this process.

An error from load is returned as is and is not stored, unless Stale.IfError answers it or Negative caches it. If the backend fails, GetOrLoad returns the result of load without storing it. Errors it works around go to Options.OnError. Invalid options return ErrInvalidOptions.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	cachedUsers := gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}}
	load := func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		fmt.Println("loading user 42")
		return User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"}, nil
	}

	for range 2 {
		u, err := gashe.GetOrLoad(ctx, c, "user:42", cachedUsers, load)
		fmt.Println(u.Name, err)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
loading user 42
Ann <nil>
Ann <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="GetOrLoadMany"></a>
## func [GetOrLoadMany](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/getorloadmany.go#L22-L28>)

```go
func GetOrLoadMany[V any](ctx context.Context, c *Cache, keys []string, o Policy[V], load func(ctx context.Context, missing []string) (map[string]V, error)) (map[string]V, error)
```

GetOrLoadMany is GetOrLoad for many keys at once, for lists and pages that would otherwise make one query per key. It reads every key in one backend call and calls load once with the keys that were missing, so the loader can fetch them in one query; what load returns is stored in one call. The result holds every key that was found or loaded; keys load leaves out are absent and not stored.

It reads entries stored by GetOrLoad with the same policy and the other way round. It supports TTL, Tags, CacheIf and Prefix; Stale, Stampede.LockFor and Negative return ErrInvalidOptions. Unlike GetOrLoad, concurrent calls do not share a load. An error from load is returned as is; if the backend fails, the result of load is returned without storing it.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	cachedUsers := gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Prefix: "user:"}

	_ = gashe.For(c, cachedUsers).Set(ctx, "1", User{ID: 1, Name: "Ann"})
	users, err := gashe.GetOrLoadMany(ctx, c, []string{"1", "2"}, cachedUsers,
		func(_ context.Context, missing []string) (map[string]User, error) {
			fmt.Println("loading", missing) // one query for every missing key
			return map[string]User{"2": {ID: 2, Name: "Bob"}}, nil
		})
	fmt.Println(users["1"].Name, users["2"].Name, err)
}
```

#### Output

```
loading [2]
Ann Bob <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Guard"></a>
## func [Guard](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/circuitbreaker.go#L220>)

```go
func Guard[T any](c *Cache, key string, o CircuitBreaker, call func() (T, error)) (T, error)
```

Guard runs call through the breaker for key, as CircuitBreaker does, and reports its error: ErrCircuitOpen while the breaker is open, otherwise what call returned.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	payments := gashe.CircuitBreaker{FailurePercent: 50, Window: time.Minute, OpenFor: 30 * time.Second}

	for range 2 {
		id, err := gashe.Guard(c, "payments", payments, func() (string, error) {
			return "", errors.New("timeout")
		})
		fmt.Printf("%q %v\n", id, err)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
"" timeout
"" gashe: circuit open
```

</p>
</details>

## func [NotNil](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L220>)

```go
func NotNil[V any](v V) bool
```

NotNil is a CacheIf rule that skips nil pointers, slices, maps, channels, functions and interfaces. Values of other kinds always pass.

<a name="Reload"></a>
## func [Reload](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/getorload.go#L67-L73>)

```go
func Reload[V any](ctx context.Context, c *Cache, key string, o Policy[V], load func(context.Context) (V, error)) (V, error)
```

Reload calls load and stores its result under key regardless of what is stored, for example after the data behind key changed. An error from load is returned and leaves the stored result alone.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	cachedUsers := gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}}

	old := func(context.Context) (User, error) { return User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"}, nil }
	renamed := func(context.Context) (User, error) { return User{ID: 42, Name: "Anna"}, nil }

	u, _ := gashe.GetOrLoad(ctx, c, "user:42", cachedUsers, old)
	fmt.Println(u.Name)
	_, _ = gashe.Reload(ctx, c, "user:42", cachedUsers, renamed) // after the rename in the database
	u, _ = gashe.GetOrLoad(ctx, c, "user:42", cachedUsers, old)
	fmt.Println(u.Name)
}
```

#### Output

```
Ann
Anna
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Backend"></a>
## type [Backend](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend.go#L17-L56>)

Backend is a place where entries live. It stores bytes only; Cache turns values into bytes.

A ttl of 0 means "no expiry" unless a method says otherwise. Methods that read a single entry return ErrNotFound on a miss. Patterns use Redis glob syntax: \*, ?, \[abc\], \[^a\], \[a\-z\] and \\ to escape. All methods must be safe for concurrent use.

```go
type Backend interface {
    // Get returns the value stored under key.
    Get(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, error)
    // GetMany returns values in the order of keys; a missing key gives a nil item.
    GetMany(ctx context.Context, keys ...string) ([][]byte, error)
    // Set stores value under key, replacing the entry and its TTL.
    Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte, ttl time.Duration) error
    // SetMany stores all values with the same TTL.
    SetMany(ctx context.Context, values map[string][]byte, ttl time.Duration) error
    // SetIfAbsent stores value only if key has no live entry and reports whether it did.
    SetIfAbsent(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte, ttl time.Duration) (stored bool, err error)
    // SetIfPresent stores value only if key has a live entry and reports whether it did.
    SetIfPresent(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte, ttl time.Duration) (stored bool, err error)
    // Delete removes key and reports whether it existed.
    Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) (existed bool, err error)
    // DeleteMany removes all keys.
    DeleteMany(ctx context.Context, keys ...string) error
    // DeleteMatch removes every key that matches pattern.
    DeleteMatch(ctx context.Context, pattern string) error
    // Scan yields every key that matches pattern. A failure is yielded once as the error, and
    // the scan stops.
    Scan(ctx context.Context, pattern string) iter.Seq2[string, error]
    // Exists reports whether key has a live entry.
    Exists(ctx context.Context, key string) (bool, error)
    // IncrBy adds by to the integer under key, creating it from 0 if absent, and returns the result.
    // ttl applies only when the entry is created.
    IncrBy(ctx context.Context, key string, by int64, ttl time.Duration) (value int64, err error)
    // Expire sets a new TTL (ttl > 0) for key and reports whether the key existed.
    Expire(ctx context.Context, key string, ttl time.Duration) (existed bool, err error)
    // TTL returns the time key has left, or NoExpiry.
    TTL(ctx context.Context, key string) (left time.Duration, err error)
    // Unlock removes key only if it holds owner and reports whether it did.
    Unlock(ctx context.Context, key string, owner []byte) (released bool, err error)
    // ExtendLock sets a new TTL (ttl > 0) for key only if it holds owner and reports whether it did.
    ExtendLock(ctx context.Context, key string, owner []byte, ttl time.Duration) (extended bool, err error)
    // Ping checks that the backend is reachable.
    Ping(ctx context.Context) error
    // Close releases resources the backend owns.
    Close() error
}
```

## type [Cache](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cache.go#L52-L63>)

Cache turns values into bytes, stores them in a Backend and runs caching, locks, rate limits and circuit breakers on top of it. It is safe for concurrent use.

```go
type Cache struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

```go

```

New returns a Cache over b. It panics if b is nil, LockPollInterval is negative or CircuitBreaker is invalid.

<a name="Cache.All"></a>

```go
func (c *Cache) All(ctx context.Context, pattern string) iter.Seq2[Value, error]
```

All yields every live entry whose key matches pattern, reading values in batches while the scan goes on. A failure is yielded once as the error.

```go
func (c *Cache) Backend() Backend
```

Backend returns the backend the cache stores bytes in, for raw access; it applies Options.Prefix and Options.CircuitBreaker.

<a name="Cache.CircuitBreaker"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [CircuitBreaker](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/circuitbreaker.go#L45>)

```go
func (c *Cache) CircuitBreaker(key string, o CircuitBreaker) (DoneFunc, error)
```

CircuitBreaker checks the breaker for key before a call to a dependency. It returns ErrCircuitOpen while the breaker is open; otherwise it returns a DoneFunc to report how the call went. The breaker lives in the memory of this process: every process judges the dependency by its own calls, and checking it costs no backend round trip.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	db := gashe.CircuitBreaker{
		FailurePercent: 50,
		Window:         time.Minute,
		OpenFor:        30 * time.Second,
	}

	for _, callErr := range []error{errors.New("timeout"), nil} {
		done, err := c.CircuitBreaker("db", db)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Println(err)
			continue
		}
		done(callErr) // report how the real call went
		fmt.Println("called, got", callErr)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
called, got timeout
gashe: circuit open
```

</p>
</details>


<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	_ = c.Set(ctx, "key", 90, 2*time.Hour)
	var n int
	err := c.Get(ctx, "key", &n)
	fmt.Println(n, err)

	err = c.Get(ctx, "missing", &n)
	fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, gashe.ErrNotFound))
}
```

#### Output

```
90 <nil>
true
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cache.IncrBy"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [IncrBy](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/values.go#L141>)

```go
func (c *Cache) IncrBy(ctx context.Context, key string, by int64, ttl time.Duration) (value int64, err error)
```

IncrBy adds by to the integer under key, creating it from 0 if absent, and returns the result. ttl applies only when the entry is created. The stored integer reads back with Get.

```go
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	for range 2 {
		n, err := c.IncrBy(ctx, "views:home", 1, 24*time.Hour) // the TTL applies on creation only
		fmt.Println(n, err)
	}
	var n int64
	_ = c.Get(ctx, "views:home", &n)
	fmt.Println(n)
}
```

#### Output

```
1 <nil>
2 <nil>
2
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cache.InvalidateTags"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [InvalidateTags](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/tags.go#L18>)

```go
func (c *Cache) InvalidateTags(ctx context.Context, tags ...string) error
```

InvalidateTags makes every result stored with one of tags a miss. Every tag has a generation counter that a result remembers when it is stored; this bumps the counters, so it costs one write per tag and no scan of the backend. Tags are shared by every process that uses the same backend.

<a name="Cache.IsLocked"></a>

```go
func (c *Cache) IsLocked(ctx context.Context, key string) (bool, error)
```

IsLocked reports whether someone holds the lock key.

<a name="Cache.Keys"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [Keys](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/values.go#L79>)

```go
func (c *Cache) Keys(ctx context.Context, pattern string) iter.Seq2[string, error]
```

Keys yields every key that matches pattern. A failure is yielded once as the error.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	_ = c.SetMany(ctx, map[string]any{"user:1": "Ann", "user:2": "Bob", "order:1": 100}, time.Hour)
	for key, err := range c.Keys(ctx, "user:*") {
		fmt.Println(key, err)
	}
}
```

<a name="Cache.Lock"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [Lock](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L28>)

```go
func (c *Cache) Lock(ctx context.Context, key string, ttl time.Duration) (*Lease, error)
```

Lock takes the lock key for ttl, waiting while someone else holds it and checking it every Options.LockPollInterval. The lock is shared by every process that uses the same backend; ttl frees it in case its holder dies. It returns ctx.Err\(\) if ctx ends first.

<a name="Cache.Ping"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [Ping](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cache.go#L108>)

```go
func (c *Cache) Ping(ctx context.Context) error
```

Ping checks that the backend is reachable.

<a name="Cache.RateLimit"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [RateLimit](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/ratelimit.go#L65>)

```go
func (c *Cache) RateLimit(ctx context.Context, key string, limit Limit) error
```

RateLimit counts a call for key and returns a \*RateLimitError, which is ErrRateLimited, once the key is over limit, across every process that uses the same backend. Call it before the work it guards. If the backend fails, it reports the error to Options.OnError and lets the call through.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	login := gashe.FixedWindow{
		Calls:  2,
		Per:    time.Minute,
		BanFor: 15 * time.Minute,
	}
	for range 3 {
		err := c.RateLimit(ctx, "login:1.2.3.4", login)
		var limited *gashe.RateLimitError
		if errors.As(err, &limited) {
			fmt.Println("429, Retry-After:", limited.RetryAfter) // errors.Is(err, gashe.ErrRateLimited) too
			continue
		}
		fmt.Println(err)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
<nil>
<nil>
429, Retry-After: 15m0s
```

</p>
</details>

```go
func (c *Cache) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, v any, ttl time.Duration) error
```

Set stores v under key. ttl 0 means no expiry; an existing entry and its TTL are replaced.

<a name="Cache.SetIfAbsent"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [SetIfAbsent](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/values.go#L32>)

```go
func (c *Cache) SetIfAbsent(ctx context.Context, key string, v any, ttl time.Duration) (stored bool, err error)
```

```go
func (c *Cache) SetIfPresent(ctx context.Context, key string, v any, ttl time.Duration) (stored bool, err error)
```

<a name="Cache.SetMany"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [SetMany](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/values.go#L63>)

```go
func (c *Cache) SetMany(ctx context.Context, values map[string]any, ttl time.Duration) error
```

<a name="Cache.Shutdown"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [Shutdown](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/shutdown.go#L12>)

```go
func (c *Cache) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
```

Shutdown stops starting background reloads and waits for the running ones to finish. If ctx is done first, it returns ctx.Err\(\) without waiting longer. Call it before closing the backend, so no reload writes to a closed one. The Cache keeps working afterwards: Stale.WhileRevalidate answers stale results without reloading them.

<a name="Cache.TTL"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [TTL](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/values.go#L157>)

```go
func (c *Cache) TTL(ctx context.Context, key string) (left time.Duration, err error)
```

TTL returns the time key has left, or NoExpiry. A miss returns ErrNotFound.

<a name="Cache.TryLock"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [TryLock](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L44>)

```go
func (c *Cache) TryLock(ctx context.Context, key string, ttl time.Duration) (lease *Lease, ok bool, err error)
```

TryLock takes the lock key for ttl if it is free; the bool is false when someone else holds it. The lock is shared by every process that uses the same backend.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	lease, ok, err := c.TryLock(ctx, "job:invoices", time.Minute)
	fmt.Println(ok, err)
	_, ok, err = c.TryLock(ctx, "job:invoices", time.Minute) // held: skip the job
	fmt.Println(ok, err)
	_ = lease.Unlock(ctx)
}
```

#### Output

```
true <nil>
false <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cache.WithLock"></a>
### func \(\*Cache\) [WithLock](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L92>)

```go
func (c *Cache) WithLock(ctx context.Context, key string, ttl time.Duration, fn func(ctx context.Context) error) error
```

WithLock runs fn while holding the lock key, waiting for it as Lock does. It extends the lock by ttl every third of ttl while fn runs, so fn may take longer than ttl, and releases it when fn returns. If the lock cannot be extended, the ctx of fn is cancelled with that error as its cause, and WithLock returns it unless fn returned an error of its own.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	// One process at a time runs the job; the lock is extended while it runs.
	err := c.WithLock(ctx, "job:invoices", time.Minute, func(context.Context) error {
		fmt.Println("sending invoices")
		return nil
	})
	fmt.Println(err)
}
```

#### Output

```
sending invoices
<nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cached"></a>
## type [Cached](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L13-L17>)

Cached is one kind of data in a Cache: a Policy bound to it, checked once. Its methods are GetOrLoad, GetOrLoadMany and Reload with that policy, plus Set and Delete that apply Policy.Prefix and store in the format GetOrLoad reads. Keep one per kind of data, such as a field of a service, and share it; it is safe for concurrent use.

```go
type Cached[V any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="For"></a>
### func [For](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L21>)

```go
func For[V any](c *Cache, o Policy[V]) Cached[V]
```

For binds o to c. It panics on invalid options, as GetOrLoad would return ErrInvalidOptions on every call.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Prefix: "user:"})
	load := func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		fmt.Println("loading user 42")
		return User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"}, nil
	}

	for range 2 {
		u, err := users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "42", load)
		fmt.Println(u.Name, err)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
loading user 42
Ann <nil>
Ann <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cached[V].Delete"></a>
### func \(Cached\[V\]\) [Delete](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L75>)

```go
func (p Cached[V]) Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) (existed bool, err error)
```

Delete removes the entry under key, with Policy.Prefix, and reports whether it existed. A read that loaded before the delete may still store its older result; tags do not have this race.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Prefix: "user:"})

	_ = users.Set(ctx, "42", User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"})
	existed, err := users.Delete(ctx, "42")
	fmt.Println(existed, err)
	existed, err = users.Delete(ctx, "42")
	fmt.Println(existed, err)
}
```

#### Output

```
true <nil>
false <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Cached[V].GetOrLoad"></a>
### func \(Cached\[V\]\) [GetOrLoad](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L30>)

```go
func (p Cached[V]) GetOrLoad(ctx context.Context, key string, load func(context.Context) (V, error)) (V, error)
```

GetOrLoad is GetOrLoad with the bound policy.

<a name="Cached[V].GetOrLoadMany"></a>
### func \(Cached\[V\]\) [GetOrLoadMany](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L35-L39>)

```go
func (p Cached[V]) GetOrLoadMany(ctx context.Context, keys []string, load func(ctx context.Context, missing []string) (map[string]V, error)) (map[string]V, error)
```

GetOrLoadMany is GetOrLoadMany with the bound policy.

<a name="Cached[V].Reload"></a>
### func \(Cached\[V\]\) [Reload](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L44>)

```go
func (p Cached[V]) Reload(ctx context.Context, key string, load func(context.Context) (V, error)) (V, error)
```

Reload is Reload with the bound policy.

<a name="Cached[V].Set"></a>
### func \(Cached\[V\]\) [Set](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cached.go#L51>)

```go
func (p Cached[V]) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, v V) error
```

Set stores v under key as GetOrLoad would store a loaded result, with the TTL, tags and shape of the policy, for example right after writing v to the database. A v that the policy does not store, by CacheIf or a negative TTL, deletes the old entry instead.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Set stores a value right after it was written to the database, so the next read is a hit.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Prefix: "user:"})

	_ = users.Set(ctx, "42", User{ID: 42, Name: "Bob"})
	u, err := users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "42", func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		fmt.Println("not called: the key is stored")
		return User{}, nil
	})
	fmt.Println(u.Name, err)
}
```

#### Output

```
Bob <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="CircuitBreaker"></a>
## type [CircuitBreaker](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/circuitbreaker.go#L18-L35>)

CircuitBreaker configures Cache.CircuitBreaker, Guard and Options.CircuitBreaker. FailurePercent, Window and OpenFor are required. Use the same options for the same key.

```go
type CircuitBreaker struct {
    // FailurePercent opens the breaker once this share of calls, from 1 to 99, failed.
    FailurePercent int
    // Window is the span of recent time calls and failures are counted over.
    Window time.Duration
    // OpenFor is how long the open breaker refuses calls.
    OpenFor time.Duration
    // MinCalls is how many calls the window needs before the breaker may open. 0 means 1.
    MinCalls int
    // HalfOpenCalls is how many test calls are let through after OpenFor: the first one that
    // succeeds closes the breaker, one that fails opens it again. 0 means the breaker just
    // closes after OpenFor.
    HalfOpenCalls int
    // IsFailure decides which errors count as failures. nil means any error; for
    // Options.CircuitBreaker, any error but ErrNotFound, ErrWrongType and a cancelled context; a
    // call whose context ended before it started is not counted.
    IsFailure func(error) bool
}
```

<a name="Codec"></a>
## type [Codec](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/codec.go#L6-L9>)

Codec turns a value into bytes and back: the format of what is stored.

```go
type Codec interface {
    Marshal(v any) ([]byte, error)
    Unmarshal(data []byte, v any) error
}
```

<a name="Compressor"></a>
## type [Compressor](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/codec.go#L13-L16>)

Compressor shrinks the bytes a Codec produced and restores them. It knows nothing of values; the packages under compress/ provide gzip and Zstandard.

```go
type Compressor interface {
    Compress(data []byte) ([]byte, error)
    Decompress(data []byte) ([]byte, error)
}
```

<a name="DoneFunc"></a>
## type [DoneFunc](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/circuitbreaker.go#L39>)

DoneFunc reports the outcome of a call that CircuitBreaker let through: nil for success, or the error the call returned. Call it once.

```go
type DoneFunc func(err error)
```

<a name="Fallback"></a>
## type [Fallback](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/fallback.go#L15-L23>)

Fallback configures Policy.Fallback: where loads keep their results while the backend of the cache fails, so the source gets one load per key and process, not one per call.

```go
type Fallback struct {
    // Backend keeps the results, usually a memory.Backend of its own; without it there is no
    // fallback. Policies of one
    // Cache may share it; a near cache or another Cache may not.
    Backend Backend
    // MaxTTL is the longest a result stays in Backend: the TTL of its policy, but never longer, since
    // no invalidation reaches Backend while the backend is down. 0 means 30 seconds.
    MaxTTL time.Duration
}
```

<a name="FixedWindow"></a>
## type [FixedWindow](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/ratelimit.go#L42-L46>)

FixedWindow allows Calls calls per window of Per that starts with the first call. The first call over the limit blocks the key for BanFor, counted from that call; 0 means Per.

```go
type FixedWindow struct {
    Calls  int
    Per    time.Duration
    BanFor time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Hooks"></a>
## type [Hooks](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cache.go#L41-L48>)

Hooks are called by the cache, for metrics and logs. A nil hook is not called.

```go
type Hooks struct {
    // OnResult receives how every GetOrLoad call, and every key of GetOrLoadMany, was answered:
    // use it to count hits and misses and to time the loader.
    OnResult func(ctx context.Context, o Outcome)
    // OnError receives errors the cache works around instead of returning them, such as a
    // failing backend during GetOrLoad; each error names the operation and key.
    OnError func(ctx context.Context, err error)
}
```

<a name="JSON"></a>
## type [JSON](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/codec.go#L48>)

JSON is the default Codec, based on encoding/json.

```go
type JSON struct{}
```

<a name="JSON.Marshal"></a>
### func \(JSON\) [Marshal](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/codec.go#L51>)

```go
func (JSON) Marshal(v any) ([]byte, error)
```

Marshal implements Codec.

<a name="JSON.Unmarshal"></a>
### func \(JSON\) [Unmarshal](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/codec.go#L54>)

```go
func (JSON) Unmarshal(data []byte, v any) error
```

Unmarshal implements Codec.

<a name="Lease"></a>
## type [Lease](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L19-L23>)

Lease is a lock held by Lock or TryLock.

```go
type Lease struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Lease.Extend"></a>
### func \(\*Lease\) [Extend](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L74>)

```go
func (l *Lease) Extend(ctx context.Context, ttl time.Duration) error
```

Extend gives the lock a new ttl from now, for work that runs longer than planned. It returns ErrLockLost if the lock expired and someone else may hold it.

<a name="Lease.Unlock"></a>
### func \(\*Lease\) [Unlock](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/lock.go#L67>)

```go
func (l *Lease) Unlock(ctx context.Context) error
```

Unlock releases the lock if it is still ours. It ignores the cancellation of ctx, so that a finished request does not leave the lock behind.

<a name="Limit"></a>
## type [Limit](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/ratelimit.go#L18-L20>)

Limit is a rate limit for Cache.RateLimit: SlidingWindow or FixedWindow.

```go
type Limit interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}
```

<a name="Negative"></a>
## type [Negative](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L93-L100>)

Negative caches loader errors that mean "there is no such data".

```go
type Negative struct {
    // IsNotFound picks the loader errors that mean "not found": answers, not failures. GetOrLoad returns
    // ErrNotFound for them, wrapping the loader error when it loaded, and alone while the answer
    // is cached; the stale result never hides them. nil turns negative caching off.
    IsNotFound func(error) bool
    // TTL is how long the negative answer is kept.
    TTL time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/cache.go#L12-L38>)

Options configures a Cache. The zero value is ready to use.

```go
type Options struct {
    // Prefix is put in front of every key the cache stores, its own keys included, so several
    // services can share one Redis: "orders:" stores "orders:user:42".
    // Keys and All yield keys without it, and DeleteMatch never reaches past it. "" means none.
    // The cache keeps its own keys, tag counters, the locks of Stampede.LockFor and
    // Stale.WhileRevalidate and rate counters, under Prefix too, each starting with "__": keys of
    // yours must not start with "__". Locks of Lock, TryLock and WithLock use the key you give them.
    Prefix string
    // Hooks receive what the cache does: how calls were answered, and the errors it works around.
    Hooks Hooks
    // CircuitBreaker stops calling the backend for a while once too many calls to it fail, as
    // Cache.CircuitBreaker does for a dependency. While it is open every call of the backend returns
    // ErrCircuitOpen at once, so a cache that is down costs no timeout: GetOrLoad goes straight to
    // the loader. The breaker lives in the memory of this process; misses are not failures, see
    // CircuitBreaker.IsFailure. Ping is not guarded, so health checks see the backend itself. The
    // zero value, with no FailurePercent, means no breaker.
    CircuitBreaker CircuitBreaker
    // Codec turns values into bytes: the format of what is stored. nil means JSON.
    Codec Codec
    // Compressor shrinks what Codec produced, such as compress/zstd for large values. nil means
    // none. Compressed values are binary: IncrBy cannot read them, so keep counters under keys
    // that only IncrBy touches.
    Compressor Compressor
    // LockPollInterval is how often Lock and Stampede.LockFor check whether a busy lock is free.
    // 0 means 100ms.
    LockPollInterval time.Duration
}
```

<details><summary>Example (On Error)</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{
		Hooks: gashe.Hooks{OnError: func(ctx context.Context, err error) {
			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "cache degraded", "error", err)
		}},
	})
	_ = c
}
```

#### Output

```

```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Prefix)</summary>

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{Prefix: "orders:"}) // several services share one Redis

	_ = c.Set(ctx, "user:42", "Ann", time.Hour)
	stored, _ := mem.Exists(ctx, "orders:user:42")
	fmt.Println(stored)
	for key, err := range c.Keys(ctx, "user:*") {
		fmt.Println(key, err)
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
true
user:42 <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Outcome"></a>
## type [Outcome](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/result.go#L9-L16>)

Outcome is what Options.OnResult receives about one answered call.

```go
type Outcome struct {
    // Key is the stored key, with Policy.Prefix.
    Key string
    // Result says how the call was answered.
    Result Result
    // Load is how long the loader ran for this call; 0 when it did not run, as on a hit.
    Load time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Policy"></a>
## type [Policy](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L16-L41>)

Policy says how GetOrLoad caches results of type V. Define it once and pass it to every call; the zero value of each field means "off".

A stored result is fresh for TTL: it is answered without calling the loader. After TTL it is stale: Stale says when it still answers, and the entry is kept for TTL plus its longest window.

```go
type Policy[V any] struct {
    // TTL says how long a result is fresh, and how much that varies.
    TTL TTL
    // Prefix is put in front of every key as is, separator included: "v2:" stores "v2:user:42".
    Prefix string
    // Stale says when a result past its TTL still answers a call: at once while it reloads,
    // instead of a failing loader, or instead of a slow one.
    Stale Stale
    // Stampede says how concurrent calls share loads, so that a key nobody has stored, or many of
    // them, do not send every caller to the source at once.
    Stampede Stampede
    // Tags lists the tags of a result; Cache.InvalidateTags of any of them makes it a miss. Tags
    // are shared by every process that uses the same backend.
    Tags []string
    // Negative caches answers like "not found", so lookups of missing data do not reach the
    // source every time.
    Negative Negative
    // Fallback keeps the results of this kind of data in a backend of its own while the backend of
    // the cache fails or its CircuitBreaker is open, for the TTL but at most Fallback.MaxTTL, and
    // answers from it (ResultFallback): the source gets one load per key and process instead of
    // one per call. The basic API and locks do not use it. Without a Backend there is none: while
    // the backend fails, every call loads.
    Fallback Fallback
    // CacheIf decides whether a result is stored. nil stores every successful result.
    CacheIf func(V) bool
}
```

<details><summary>Example (Fallback)</summary>
<p>

Fallback keeps results in a memory backend of its own; while the backend of the cache fails, calls are answered from it instead of loading every time.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	spare := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer spare.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{
		TTL:      gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour},
		Fallback: gashe.Fallback{Backend: spare, MaxTTL: time.Minute},
	})
	u, err := users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "user:42", func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		return User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"}, nil
	})
	fmt.Println(u.Name, err)
}
```

#### Output

```
Ann <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Max Concurrent Loads)</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	reports := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[string]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Stampede: gashe.Stampede{MaxLoads: 1}})

	started, release := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		_, _ = reports.GetOrLoad(ctx, "a", func(context.Context) (string, error) {
			close(started)
			<-release // a slow query holds the only slot
			return "a", nil
		})
	}()
	<-started

	waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := reports.GetOrLoad(waitCtx, "b", func(context.Context) (string, error) { return "b", nil })
	fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, gashe.ErrOverloaded), err)
	close(release)
	<-done
}
```

#### Output

```
true gashe: overloaded: context deadline exceeded
```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Negative)</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	errNoUser := errors.New("no such user") // such as sql.ErrNoRows
	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{
		TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour},
		Negative: gashe.Negative{
			IsNotFound: func(err error) bool { return errors.Is(err, errNoUser) },
			TTL:        time.Minute,
		},
	})
	load := func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		fmt.Println("querying the database")
		return User{}, errNoUser
	}

	for range 2 {
		_, err := users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "user:404", load)
		fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, gashe.ErrNotFound)) // from the loader, then from the cache
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
querying the database
true
true
```

```go
package main

import (

	fmt.Println(v, err)
	time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // past TTL: the next call loads
	v, err = rates.GetOrLoad(ctx, "usd", func(context.Context) (float64, error) {
		return 0, errors.New("rates API is down")
```

<details><summary>Example (Stale While Revalidate)</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	prices := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[int]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Millisecond}, Stale: gashe.Stale{WhileRevalidate: time.Hour}})

	var version atomic.Int64
	load := func(context.Context) (int, error) { return int(version.Add(1)), nil }

	v, _ := prices.GetOrLoad(ctx, "price", load)
	fmt.Println(v)
	time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // past TTL: the stored price is stale
	v, _ = prices.GetOrLoad(ctx, "price", load)
	fmt.Println(v, "answered at once, reloading in the background")
	_ = c.Shutdown(ctx) // waits for the background reload
	v, _ = prices.GetOrLoad(ctx, "price", load)
	fmt.Println(v)
}
```

#### Output

```
1
1 answered at once, reloading in the background
2
```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Tags)</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

type User struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})
	users := gashe.For(c, gashe.Policy[User]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Hour}, Tags: []string{"users"}})
	load := func(context.Context) (User, error) {
		fmt.Println("loading")
		return User{ID: 42, Name: "Ann"}, nil
	}

	_, _ = users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "user:42", load)
	_, _ = users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "user:42", load) // a hit
	_ = c.InvalidateTags(ctx, "users")           // every result tagged "users" is now a miss
	_, _ = users.GetOrLoad(ctx, "user:42", load)
}
```

```
loading
loading
```

<details><summary>Example (Ttl)</summary>
<p>

TTL takes a time.Duration, a string for time.ParseDuration or a function of the result.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	type Token struct {
		Value     string
		ExpiresIn time.Duration
	}
	load := func(context.Context) (Token, error) { return Token{Value: "t", ExpiresIn: 5 * time.Minute}, nil }

	ttlOf := func(t Token) time.Duration { return t.ExpiresIn - time.Minute }
	for key, ttl := range map[string]any{
		"duration": time.Hour,
		"string":   "1h30m", // such as a value from the configuration
		"func":     ttlOf,   // from the result
		"int":      3600,    // not a time.Duration: an error
	} {
		_, err := gashe.GetOrLoad(ctx, c, key, gashe.Policy[Token]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: ttl}}, load)
		left, _ := c.TTL(ctx, key)
		fmt.Printf("%s: %v %v\n", key, left.Round(time.Minute), errors.Is(err, gashe.ErrInvalidOptions))
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
duration: 1h0m0s false
string: 1h30m0s false
func: 4m0s false
int: 0s true
```

</p>

```go
type Result int
```

<a name="ResultHit"></a>

```go
const (
    // ResultHit is a fresh stored result.
    ResultHit Result = iota + 1
    // ResultMiss means the loader ran.
    ResultMiss
    // ResultStaleWhileRevalidate is a stale stored result, answered while it is reloaded in the
    // background.
    ResultStaleWhileRevalidate
    // ResultStaleIfError is a stale stored result, answered instead of a loader error.
    ResultStaleIfError
    // ResultNegativeHit is a cached negative answer.
    ResultNegativeHit
    // ResultStaleIfSlow is a stale stored result, answered because the loader took longer than
    // Stale.IfSlow.After; the load goes on in the background.
    ResultStaleIfSlow
    // ResultFallback is a result kept in Policy.Fallback, answered while the backend fails.
    ResultFallback
)
```

## type [SlidingWindow](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/ratelimit.go#L26-L29>)

SlidingWindow allows about Calls calls in any span of Per. It keeps two counters per key, for the current and the last fixed window of Per, and weighs the last one by how much of it still falls inside the sliding window, as if its calls were spread evenly. Refused calls are not counted.

```go
type SlidingWindow struct {
    Calls int
    Per   time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Stale"></a>
## type [Stale](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L104-L113>)

Stale says when a stored result past its TTL, the stale result, still answers a call. Each way has its own window after TTL; the zero value of each is off.

```go
type Stale struct {
    // WhileRevalidate is how long after TTL the stale result answers at once, while one caller
    // reloads it in the background (stale-while-revalidate of RFC 5861). The refresh lock is
    // shared by every process that uses the same backend.
    WhileRevalidate time.Duration
    // IfError answers a failing loader with the stale result.
    IfError StaleIfError
    // IfSlow answers a slow loader with the stale result.
    IfSlow StaleIfSlow
}
```

<a name="StaleIfError"></a>
## type [StaleIfError](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L117-L123>)

StaleIfError answers a loader error with the stale result \(stale\-if\-error of RFC 5861\), so callers keep getting data while the source is down.

```go
type StaleIfError struct {
    // For is how long after TTL the stale result answers a failure. 0 turns it off.
    For time.Duration
    // IsFailure picks the loader errors that are failures. nil means any error. An error
    // Negative.IsNotFound accepts is never one: it is the answer "not found".
    IsFailure func(error) bool
}
```

<a name="StaleIfSlow"></a>
## type [StaleIfSlow](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L128-L133>)

StaleIfSlow answers a slow loader with the stale result: the call waits at most After, then gets the stale result while the load goes on in the background and stores what it gets; meanwhile other calls of the key get the stale result at once.

```go
type StaleIfSlow struct {
    // For is how long after TTL the stale result answers a slow loader. 0 turns it off.
    For time.Duration
    // After is how long a call waits for the loader before the stale result answers it.
    After time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Stampede"></a>
## type [Stampede](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L74-L90>)

Stampede says how concurrent calls share loads: within this process with SingleFlight, across processes with LockFor, and how many loads of one kind run at once with MaxLoads. They work together: with SingleFlight the calls of a process share one load first, and only that load takes the lock of LockFor.

```go
type Stampede struct {
    // SingleFlight makes concurrent calls for one key and type in this process share one lookup and
    // one load. The load runs with the ctx values of the call that started it: leave it off when
    // the loader reads from ctx what the key does not name, such as the user of the request.
    SingleFlight bool
    // LockFor, when set, makes a missing key load under a lock: one process calls the loader, the
    // others wait and take its result. The lock is shared by every process that uses the same
    // backend, and LockFor is the longest it is held, so a process that dies holding it frees it.
    LockFor time.Duration
    // MaxLoads is how many loads of this kind of data, its type and Prefix, may run at once in
    // this process: with 10 processes, up to 10 times as many reach the source. A call over the
    // limit waits for a slot as long as its ctx allows, then returns ErrOverloaded; one that the
    // stale result can answer, within Stale.IfError or Stale.IfSlow or a background reload, does
    // not wait. The wait has no limit but ctx: give calls a deadline, or calls over the limit pile
    // up. Use the same value for the same kind of data. 0 means no limit.
    MaxLoads int
}
```

<a name="TTL"></a>
## type [TTL](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/policy.go#L44-L68>)

TTL says how long a result is fresh.

```go
type TTL struct {
    // For is how long a result is fresh: a time.Duration, a string for time.ParseDuration such
    // as "1h", or a func(V) time.Duration of the result type that picks it from the result; to
    // leave a result out, use CacheIf, not a negative TTL:
    //
    //	For: time.Hour
    //	For: 90 * time.Second
    //	For: "1h30m"
    //	For: cfg.UserTTL // a string from the configuration, such as "10m"
    //	For: func(t Token) time.Duration { return time.Until(t.ExpiresAt) - time.Minute }
    //	For: func(u User) time.Duration {
    //		if u.Admin {
    //			return time.Minute // admins change often
    //		}
    //		return time.Hour
    //	}
    //
    // Any other type, a plain int such as 3600 included, returns ErrInvalidOptions. For may be
    // left out when a window of Stale is set: then every call either refreshes in the background
    // (Stale.WhileRevalidate) or calls the loader (Stale.IfError, Stale.IfSlow).
    For any
    // Jitter spreads TTLs randomly by up to this share, from 0 to 1 (0.1 means +-10%), so that
    // entries stored together do not expire together.
    Jitter float64
}
```
